coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 9 units (the domain root directory plus 11.01-11.08) and 52 files, matching the expected counts exactly. Every file was read in full. Dimension applicability: Problem Clarity (1) and Persona Specificity (2) are N/A throughout - the problem statement and the four ratified personas are owned by meta/ and are referenced, never redefined, under D-19; the Role Matrix/Role Lens surfaces here are consumers of that artifact, not definitions of it. Constraint Explicitness (4) and Competitive Positioning (6) are applicable only to the domain root unit, which carries the 'Not-Product Concerns Routed Out' NFR table and the named-competitor rationale (Musicbed, Artlist, Songtradr, Epidemic, Jaxsta); sub-domain units neither own nor are expected to own those axes. Dimensions 3, 5, 7 and 8 are applicable to all nine units. The 4 broken cross-domain directory links physically sit in 11.02, 11.05 and 11.08 but are reported once against the domain root as a single domain-wide structural defect, and dimension 8 is scored down only at the root for them, to avoid triple-counting one defect. Six candidate findings were raised in 3a and dropped in 3c after following cross-references that resolved them: the creator whitelist-failure 'blocks or loudly flags' either/or (resolved by 11.08.02 D-06 and its explicit reconciliation at lines 83-84 that the licence stands and 11.06.01 D-02 describes the purchase experience only); rev-share stacking past 100% (resolved by 11.08.02 line 126, 'Refused at 11.05.03 D-03, before issuance'); the AI-training default inversion flagged as a latent contradiction by the domain CX P-04/CX-17 (resolved by 11.04.02 D-12 and its Defaults section, which state the inversion explicitly); the stale [PENDING] markers in 11.01-cx CX-05 Q2, 11.02-cx CX-05 Q5, 11.04-cx CX-01 Q4 and 11.05-cx CX-03 Q5 (each answered normatively in a child - 11.01.04 line 52, 11.02.03 D-02, 11.04.02 D-06, 11.05.04 Q-03 respectively); 11.10's unmodelled karaoke edge case (the feature is banded WONT, so no implementer is forced to invent anything); and the '(D-10)' mis-citation for chain-of-title at 11.01.03 line 15 (a citation slip that does not change what gets built).

units.note: Dimension 5 is N/A: the domain index asserts no success metric and is not the artifact that owns them. Dimension 7 WARN for two bare [PENDING] markers with neither owner nor deferral target; the Open Questions tables themselves are exemplary. Dimension 8 WARN for a stale Children-table Status column, an internally inconsistent Deep Think total, and four dead cross-domain directory links.

Dimension 3 carries two independent blocking defects in the verdict model; scored WARN rather than FAIL because the rubric's FAIL criterion ('missing MoSCoW or major features absent') is not met - the defects are contradictions inside a fully-enumerated feature, and their severity is carried by the findings.

Dimension 3 FAIL: the domain's shared type system (11.08.01) is defined with nine axes in the file that owns it and enumerated as six in five other files including two [DEEP] siblings and the domain CX, and the instrument's version-pinning moment is stated two ways citing the same decision id. Both are definitional defects in a load-bearing feature, not edge-case gaps.

findings.claim: The licence scope grammar has nine axes in the [DEEP] file that owns it and six axes in every other file that enumerates it, including two [DEEP] siblings and the domain cross-cut file. Load-bearing decisions in 11.04 and the domain CX are built on the absence of three of the nine axes, so the two readings cannot both hold.
findings.evidence: 11.08.01-licence-scope-grammar.md:45-55 defines nine axes - 'Media', 'Data use', 'Territory', 'Term', 'Exclusivity', 'Usage', 'Scale', 'Extent of use', 'Grantee scope' - and 11.08.01:104 resolves a request point with all nine: 'media:{podcast} · territory:{249 codes, label "worldwide"} · term:{trigger: on-issue, duration: perpetual} · exclusivity: none · usage:{in-context} · scale:{band 2} · extent:{full track, 1 use} · grantee:{Buyer Ltd, no sublicence} · data-use: none'. 11.08.01 D-15 (line 229): '**Grantee scope is an axis** - licensee plus permitted assignees/sublicensees, bounded by a stated purpose.' 11.08.01 D-06 (line 220): '**Data use (AI training) is a separate axis, defaults to none, and is never implied by any media grant however broad**'. Against that: 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md D-09 (line 240) - 'the grammar has no counterparty axis (11.08.01), so buyer blocks cannot fold (11.04.03)'; 11.04.02 DT-07 (line 199) - '**the scope grammar has no counterparty axis** (11.08.01: media, territory, term, exclusivity, usage, scale)'; music-licensing-cx.md CX-16 (line 146) - 'the grammar's six axes (media/territory/term/exclusivity/usage/scale) contain **no counterparty axis**'; 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:46 - 'A scope is a point in the 11.08.01 grammar (media, territory, term, exclusivity, usage, scale)'; 11.03.01-rate-cards-pricing-rules.md:26 - 'Scope uses the licence grammar from 11.08.01 (media, territory, term, exclusivity, usage, category)'; 11.04.01-per-work-licensing-policy.md:31 - 'Its key space is the licence scope grammar (11.08.01): media, territory, term, exclusivity, usage, scale'.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent which axis set is authoritative, and therefore whether the clearance gate's scope object carries a `data use` axis and a `grantee scope` axis at all.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer submits an AI-training request. Under the six-axis enumeration that 11.02.01:46 gives the gate, there is no `data use` axis, so training must be expressed as a media value - which 11.08.01 DT-04 (line 172) identifies as silently inverting 11.07.01 D-01 ('opt-in, never opt-out; silence is refusal') for every owner who ever set a broad media grant, and which 11.04.02:80-81 calls 'the single most damaging bug available in this domain'. Separately, under the nine-axis reading the `grantee scope` axis exists, which falsifies the stated rationale for 11.04.02 D-09's two-key-spaces model and for 11.04.01 Q-05's rejection of buyer allow-lists ('buyer identity sits outside the scope grammar's axes'), so two ratified decisions rest on a premise the owning file contradicts.

findings.claim: The moment at which an instrument pins its grammar version is stated as 'request creation' in the file that owns the rule and as 'at issue' in three places in two other files - and all four cite the same decision id, 11.08.01 D-03.
findings.evidence: 11.08.01-licence-scope-grammar.md D-03 (line 217): '**Instances pin the grammar version at *request creation*** and carry it unchanged through pricing to issue | **Refines the breadth pass's "pins at issue"**, which raced 11.03.01 D-02 (card pins at read): a v4-priced quote could issue under v5 and the certificate's scope would not be the scope quoted.' 11.08.01 Cross-Cut Notes (line 192) instructs the sibling directly: 'it must carry `grammarVersion` pinned at **request**, not at issue (D-03 refinement, DT-13).' Against that: 11.08.02-licence-certificate-issuance.md:55 - 'Grammar version | Pinned at issue (11.08.01 D-03)'; 11.08.02:145 - 'Grammar gains/changes an axis between quote and issue | The instrument pins the version **in force at issue** (11.08.01 D-03). If the agreed scope is not expressible in that version, **abort**'; 11.08-licence-instrument-lifecycle-cx.md:34 - 'Instances pin the grammar version at issue'; 11.08-...-cx.md:38 - 'Grammar version pinned at issue. Same rule as 11.03.01 D-02 (card pins at read).' 11.08.02 was last updated 2026-07-23, after 11.08.01 (2026-07-16), so the stale reading is the later text.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the pinning moment, and must decide whether 11.08.02's 'abort if the agreed scope is not expressible in the current version' path exists at all.
findings.failureScenario: A quote is composed and priced on 12 March under grammar v4. The platform ships v5 on 20 March, splitting the media axis. The buyer accepts on 25 March. Under 11.08.01 D-03 the request pinned v4 and the certificate serialises the scope the buyer was quoted. Under 11.08.02:55/:145 and 11.08-cx:34/:38 the instrument pins v5 and either re-maps the scope or aborts the accepted deal - producing exactly the price/permission mismatch on an irrevocable instrument that 11.08.01 DT-13 was written to design out and that 11.03.01 D-02 calls 'fraud, not a race condition'.

findings.claim: Two features state that an undeclared work cannot be one-stop, but the verdict model that owns the one-stop determination has no input and no verdict value that distinguishes 'no encumbrances exist' from 'nobody has said whether any exist'. Its four-input evaluation returns clearable-now for a work nobody has ever asked.
findings.evidence: 11.02.03-encumbrance-declaration.md D-02 (line 207): 'Silence is not cleanliness - an undeclared work is not one-stop', with the States table (line 158) making it the feature's core: '**"Nothing declared" - not "clean".** The distinction is the entire feature', and the edge case at line 126: 'Nobody declares anything - silence | **Silence must not mean clean.**' rendered to the user as 'No sample declaration - this work can't be one-stop. [Declare]'. 11.05.01-sample-declaration-identification.md D-05 (line 238) and its States table (line 187) restate it: '**Empty - negative** | Asked, answered "nothing borrowed" | **A different state from the above**, and only this one can support one-stop via 11.02.02.' Against that, 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:92 lists the whole evaluation: 'shares close -> a valid, uncontested completeness attestation exists (11.02.02) -> **no encumbrance in this work or any ancestor** (11.02.03) -> the effective work policy (11.04.03 fold) permits this scope' - an empty encumbrance set passes. Its verdict table (lines 63-70) has six values and defines `incomplete` narrowly as 'The record is not closed - shares do not sum, or no valid completeness attestation exists', which is about the party list, not about borrowing. A grep of 11.02.01 for 'declar' returns only Role Lens prose and DT-14; the file states no declaration-presence requirement anywhere, and has no edge case mirroring its own 'Shares sum to 100% but no completeness attestation exists -> incomplete' row (line 103) for the declaration side.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent a verdict value (or an out-of-band gate) for 'no declaration has been made', and its remedy owner, since 11.02.01 D-09 requires every verdict to name exactly one.
findings.failureScenario: A solo producer uploads a finished track, attests the writer and master lists, sets a permissive policy, and never answers the borrowing prompt. Implementer A follows 11.02.01's four inputs: the encumbrance set is empty, so the verdict is `clearable-now` and the work is badged one-stop. Implementer B follows 11.02.03 D-02 and withholds one-stop. The two builds disagree on the domain's headline signal for the most common cold-start work, and A ships the badge on the least-verified catalogue - the exact outcome 11.02.01 DT-14 rejects.

findings.claim: A verified non-listed authorship claim must block new issuance without invalidating the attestation, but the gate's only route to blocking is verdict `incomplete`, which is defined as 'no valid completeness attestation exists'. The attestation would have to be simultaneously valid and non-existent.
findings.evidence: 11.02.02-catalogue-completeness-attestation.md D-12 (line 209): '**A listed party's contest invalidates immediately; a non-listed party's claim marks the work `contested` and blocks new issuance without auto-invalidating**', with the edge case at line 130 spelling out the mechanism: 'Does **not** auto-invalidate ... Work moves to `contested`: visible to buyers, the **gate blocks new issuance** (11.02.01 D-04 re-evaluates fresh), issued licences stand', and a `Contested` row in its States table (line 158). 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:122 collapses both contest species into one rule: '**Attestation is contested mid-gate** | Contest wins immediately; verdict -> `incomplete`; issuance refused.' Its verdict table (line 68) defines `incomplete` as 'The record is not closed - shares do not sum, or no valid completeness attestation exists', and its precedence list D-08 (line 194) is a closed six-value enum with no `contested`. A grep of 11.02.01 for 'contest' returns only line 92, line 122, DT-08's unrelated hold contention, and one cross-cut note - no verdict, no remedy owner (D-09 assigns one per verdict and has no entry for a claim), and no buyer-facing rendering.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent how the gate expresses 'valid attestation, open third-party claim, refuse issuance' - a seventh verdict, a side-channel boolean, or a deliberate misuse of `incomplete` or `unknown`.
findings.failureScenario: A verified non-listed claimant asserts a share in a work whose attestation is valid and uncontested by any listed party. Implementer A maps it to `incomplete` per 11.02.01:122, which tells the owner 'nobody has confirmed the writer list is complete' when someone has, and routes the remedy to 11.02.02 ('attest') - an action that cannot clear the claim. Implementer B maps it to `unknown`, which routes escalation to domain 09 instead of the dispute path 11.02.02 D-12 requires. Implementer C treats it as a gate-only flag outside the verdict, so search still badges the work `clearable-now` while checkout refuses it, contradicting 11.02.01 D-16's rule that search is an advisory snapshot of the same verdict.

findings.claim: Buyer blocks are stated to be unfoldable and evaluable only at request time, but no file says which component evaluates them or what result they produce. The fold excludes them by construction and the clearance verdict consumes only the fold and takes no buyer parameter, so nothing in the specified pipeline enforces a buyer block.
findings.evidence: 11.04.02-co-owner-veto-approval.md D-09 (line 240): '**Two key spaces**: category blocks key on the scope grammar and take effect at authoring time, catalogue-wide; buyer blocks key on party identity and can only be evaluated at request time', with its shapes table (line 63) confirming 'Buyer (never this company) | **Party identity** (domain 01) - *not* an axis of the scope grammar | **At request time only.**' music-licensing-cx.md CX-18 (line 29): 'The fold operates over the grammar and therefore **cannot fold buyer blocks** ... the effective-work-policy aggregate is incomplete by construction.' 11.04.03-policy-conflict-resolution.md never mentions buyer blocks at all; its Behavior (line 26-36) folds 'every individual share policy and every veto' over the grammar, and its D-08 (line 115) states '11.02.01 consumes this fold's verdict and the per-request binding-owner answer, never the individual share policies'. 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:49-57 lists the verdict's five inputs - consent graph, attestation, encumbrance set, 'The effective work policy (11.04.03) ... Consumes the aggregate, never the individual policies', and required rights sides - none of which carries a buyer identity; its happy path (line 89) takes a scope and never a buyer. 11.04.01-per-work-licensing-policy.md:37 names only 'Refusal (11.04.02 veto / category block)' as evaluation step 1.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent where a buyer block is evaluated, whether the gate re-checks it at issuance, and what verdict or refusal object it produces.
findings.failureScenario: An owner blocks BrandCo. BrandCo requests a licence. The fold (11.04.03) cannot see the block, and the gate (11.02.01) consumes only the fold and never receives a buyer identity, so the verdict is `clearable-now` and 11.08.02's preconditions are satisfied. The licence issues to the blocked buyer and is irrevocable under domain D-06 - directly defeating 11.04.02 D-15's claim that 'No window exists in which a blocked scope passes the gate'.

findings.claim: For two buyers concurrently seeking an exclusive-scope licence on one work, 11.01.05 says the second is queued; 11.02.01 D-12 and 11.01-cx CX-03 say the second is refused and explicitly forbid queueing. 'Queue' also has a defined technical meaning in this sub-domain (second-call holds), so the word is not loose.
findings.evidence: 11.01.05-dual-licence-coordination.md:64: 'Two buyers request an exclusive-scope licence on the same work at once (concurrency) | The hold (11.01.04) is the arbiter - first request to place a valid hold spanning both sides wins; **the second is queued behind the hold**, not silently lost'. Against that: 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md D-12 (line 198): '**At most one exclusive licence per (work, exclusivity scope) can ever exist.** A concurrent second exclusive attempt is refused, not queued ... Queueing sells a buyer a wait for a certainty they cannot get', restated in its edge case at line 115 ('Second attempt is **refused, not queued** (D-12)') and in 11.08.02-licence-certificate-issuance.md:123 ('**First to commit wins; the second is refused, never queued**'). 11.01-sync-licensing-cx.md CX-03 synthesis Q1 (line 36): 'If two exclusive holds are attempted concurrently, the hold record is the serialization point and **the second must fail closed, not queue**.' 11.01.04-holds-exclusivity-windows.md:33 gives 'queue' a defined meaning in this feature - '**second-call** queues behind a first-call' - and its own concurrency row (line 51) says 'the second fails closed. Never both-granted.'
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether the losing buyer gets a durable waitlist position that can auto-grant on release, or only a notify-me subscription.
findings.failureScenario: Buyer B loses the race for an exclusive hold. Implementer A, reading 11.01.05:64, registers B's request as a queued second-call behind an exclusive hold - a state 11.01.04's own hold-type model does not define, and one that promises B a position 11.02.01 D-12 says cannot exist. Implementer B, reading CX-03 and D-12, fails B's request closed and offers only a notification. The two builds give the same buyer materially different rights over the same slot.

findings.claim: The open question 'does a work with a dead, erased or permanently unreachable co-owner sit non-one-stop forever, and is that acceptable?' was withdrawn from 11.02.02, handed to 11.02.04, and never landed - while two files still route readers to the withdrawn question's id, which has since been reused for an unrelated question.
findings.evidence: 11.02.02-catalogue-completeness-attestation.md DT-07 (line 171) withdraws it: 'The old Q-04 ("do those works sit non-one-stop forever?") assumed a gate that D-04 removes; it is withdrawn', and its Cross-Cut Notes (line 181) hand the residue on: 'The estate/unreachable-party problem DT-07 hands off lands here [11.02.04]'. The Q-04 slot in that file is now a different question entirely - line 218: 'Q-04 | **Does a verified non-listed authorship claim drop one-stop, or only mark the work `contested`?**' But 11.02.04-multi-party-consent-routing.md:66 still routes there: 'A party is unreachable / dead / erased | Permanently non-one-stop for scopes needing them | See 11.02.01 Q-03 and **11.02.02 Q-04**', and 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md:120 does the same: 'This is common, not exotic (11.02.02 Q-04).' 11.02.04's own Open Questions table (lines 111-113) contains no row owning the unreachable-party remedy; its Q-01 covers a *reachable* holdout ('The live owner choice is therefore **buyout/negotiation surface vs nothing**'), which presupposes a counterparty who can be bought out.
findings.forcedInvention: None at the behaviour level - 11.02.01 D-17 fixes the mechanics. What is missing is any tracked owner for the product decision on whether permanent non-clearability for an unreachable party is acceptable, and what the interim story is.
findings.failureScenario: A reader hitting 11.02.04's dead/erased row follows the pointer to 11.02.02 Q-04 and lands on a non-listed-authorship-claim question that says nothing about unreachable parties. The handoff 11.02.02 line 181 declares was made has no destination row, so a decision the two files agree is open is owned by nobody and will not surface at /create-prd.

findings.claim: D-15 gates a buyer-facing time-to-clear estimate on a party having 'a response history' / having 'responded enough times to have one', without a number - and this threshold is untracked, while its direct sibling (the minimum cohort size for owner-facing search standing) is explicitly tracked as an open question.
findings.evidence: 11.02.01-clearance-computation-one-stop.md D-15 (line 201): 'Time-to-clear is shown only where derived: `instant` for policy-covered scopes; **a per-party historical median where that party has a response history**; "unknown", stated plainly, otherwise. Never a point estimate for a party with no history.' DT-10 (line 155) gives the same rule with the same softness: 'a per-party historical median where that party has **responded enough times to have one**'. No open question in 11.02.01 or its parent index covers the threshold - Q-01, Q-03 and Q-06 are legal/business posture, Q-04, Q-05 and Q-07 are resolved. Compare 11.01.02-supervisor-search-reference-matching.md Q-03 (line 108), which tracks the structurally identical parameter explicitly: 'What is left is the two parameters: the minimum cohort size below which standing is suppressed, and the delay window ... routed exactly as its precedents ... to `/create-prd-security`.'
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the minimum number of prior responses at which a party's median becomes publishable as an ETA.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A shows a median after two prior responses; implementer B requires ten. Under D-15's own reasoning an ETA is 'the number a supervisor commits an air date against', so A ships a fabricated-feeling estimate off a two-point sample - the fabrication DT-10 rejects - while B shows 'unknown' for parties who have demonstrably answered, degrading the feature the buyer cares most about.

findings.claim: 11.08.01 D-08 requires the lifecycle feature to treat a term with no computable end as first-class, but 11.08.04's expiry model is a single T-minus-N countdown with no handling for a term whose expiry is ~249 different dates, and no open question owns the gap.
findings.evidence: 11.08.01-licence-scope-grammar.md D-08 (line 222): 'A term may have **no computable expiry date** | ... "life of copyright" ~249 dates worldwide ... **11.08.04 must treat "no computable end" as first-class**', with the edge case at line 128 stating the arithmetic: '**"Life of copyright, worldwide"** | Has **~249 different expiry dates** - life+70 in the EU/UK, life+100 in Mexico, 95-from-publication for US works-for-hire. There is **no single expiry date**', and its Cross-Cut Notes (line 194) listing it as case (a) landing on 11.08.04. 11.08.04-licence-amendment-expiry-lifecycle.md carries none of it: its Behavior (line 35) says only 'Expiry - a term ends. Automatic, unattended, and it must warn **both** sides'; D-03 (line 103) is 'Expiry warns the owner as well as the buyer'; its edge case (line 58) is 'Warning at T-minus-N to both sides; expiry is not a surprise'; its only non-standard case is 'Perpetual licence (creator, 11.06.04) | No expiry' (line 64). Its Open Questions (lines 111-113) cover wrongly-issued licences, the supersede-never-edit invariant, and narrowing amendments - none the multi-date term. 11.08.04 was last updated 2026-07-17, after 11.08.01 (2026-07-16).
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a worldwide life-of-copyright licence expires per-territory on ~249 dates, on the earliest of them, on the latest, or never - and which date the T-minus-N warnings count back from.
findings.failureScenario: A worldwide life-of-copyright sync issues. Implementer A schedules expiry on the earliest territory date, silently truncating the buyer's rights in the other 248 territories decades early on an irrevocable instrument. Implementer B schedules on the latest, so the licence continues to verify as valid in territories where the copyright has lapsed. Implementer C schedules nothing, and D-03's owner-side renewal warning - which 11.08.04 DT-02 calls a seller-side revenue event - never fires at all.

findings.claim: Open items are deferred to `/ideate-discover` Step 5, a stage the tree elsewhere records as completed, with no owner named. In at least two places the substance is not answered by any child or open question, so the item is tracked to a run that has already finished without recording an answer.
findings.evidence: 11.07.03-training-compensation-attribution.md:57: 'Rights holder wants attribution but not money | Plausible and unsupported by a payment-shaped feature | `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' - no owner, and no open question in that file covers it (Q-01/Q-02 are the division basis and the stem rate; Q-03 is a domain-placement call between 02 and 11; Q-04 is manifest-vs-current split). 11.08-licence-instrument-lifecycle-cx.md:57 is the second: 'Should a party who previously verified be notified when the licence changes? It would require tracking who asked, which turns an anonymous check into a surveillance record. `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' - and neither 11.08.03 (Q-01 public-vs-authenticated, Q-02 disclosure tiers, Q-03 use-level verification) nor 11.08.04 carries it. The tree records the stage as run: 11.03.01-rate-cards-pricing-rules.md Q-03 (line 100) states '**Deferral expired** - `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and did not answer it', and 11.10-print-lyric-rights.md Q-02/Q-03 show the repair pattern applied elsewhere - '**Deferral target re-pointed** from the completed `/ideate-validate` run (2026-07-18, which closed without recording an answer)'.
findings.forcedInvention: None directly; the defect is that two live product questions are parked against a stage that cannot answer them and against no owner, so they will not reach /create-prd.
findings.failureScenario: The pipeline advances to /create-prd. Both items are invisible to it - they are not rows in any Open Questions table and their stated destination has already run - so an implementer of 11.07.03 has no answer for a rights holder who consents but declines payment, and an implementer of 11.08.03 must decide unilaterally whether to build a verifier-notification register that CX-04 itself flags as turning an anonymous check into a surveillance record.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table reports every child as `[SURFACE]` and states the depth pass has not run, while nine leaf files are `[DEEP]`, twenty-two are `[PARTIAL]` and all eight sub-domain indexes are `[BREADTH]`. The same table's stated Deep Think total does not equal the sum of its own rows.
findings.evidence: music-licensing-index.md:40: '> All `[SURFACE]` - breadth pass only; depth is allocated by MoSCoW in `/ideate-discover` Step 5.' followed by lines 44-54, whose Status column reads `[SURFACE]` for all eleven children. On disk: 11.02-clearance-one-stop-status-index.md:5, 11.04-...-index.md:5, 11.05-...-index.md:5 and 11.08-...-index.md:5 all read '**Status**: [BREADTH]', and nine leaf files read '**Status**: [DEEP]' (11.02.01, 11.02.02, 11.02.03, 11.04.01, 11.04.02, 11.05.01, 11.08.01, 11.08.02). The depth pass demonstrably ran: music-licensing-cx.md:5 - '**Status**: [DEEP] - 8 sub-domains + 3 features; intra-domain cross-cuts mapped and synthesised **after the deepening pass**' - and 11.03.01-rate-cards-pricing-rules.md Q-03 (line 100) - '`/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run'. Separately, music-licensing-index.md:56 states '**Totals**: 8 sub-domains · 34 leaf features · **187 Deep Think hypotheses logged** · max depth 3': the sub-domain and leaf-feature counts sum exactly from the table above it (5+4+3+3+5+4+3+4 = 31, +3 = 34), but the Deep Think column sums to 103 (15+13+9+9+15+12+9+12+3+3+3), not 187. 187 is the correct post-depth count of DT rows on disk, so the per-row figures are breadth-era and the total is current, inside one table.
findings.forcedInvention: None; this is a structure-map integrity defect.
findings.failureScenario: A downstream workflow that reads the pipeline key file to decide what still needs deepening sees eleven `[SURFACE]` children and an explicit 'breadth pass only' note, and either re-runs discovery over nine files that are already [DEEP] or reports the domain as un-deepened. The self-inconsistent totals in the same table give a reader no way to tell which column is current.

findings.claim: Four cross-domain references in three sub-domains point at directory names that do not exist in the ideation tree, so following them yields nothing.
findings.evidence: 11.02.02-catalogue-completeness-attestation.md:189 - 'Touches **08 Real-Time Jamming** ([path](../../08-real-time-jamming/))'; the directory is `08-realtime-jamming-remote-sessions/`. 11.05.01-sample-declaration-identification.md:222 - 'Touches **02 Credits & Verified Work History** ([path](../../02-credits-work-history/))'; the directory is `02-credits-attribution/`, which the same tree cites correctly at 11.02.01:174 and 11.07.03:85. 11.05.01:226 - 'Touches **01 Identity & Entities** ([path](../../01-identity-entities/))'; the directory is `01-identity-profiles-organizations/`. 11.08.02-licence-certificate-issuance.md:201 - 'Touches **01 Identity & Profiles** ([path](../../01-identity-profiles/))'; same target, also wrong. A resolution pass over every `../../NN-*/` link emitted from this domain returns exactly these four as MISSING and eighteen as OK; every relative `.md` link in the domain resolves.
findings.forcedInvention: None; this is a reference-integrity defect.
findings.failureScenario: A spec writer resolving 11.05.01 D-06's stated hard dependency - 'declaration attaches to the contribution, not the work ... Hard dependency on domain 07's contribution graph' - follows the adjacent entity-resolution link for a band-as-source and gets a dead path, so the domain 01 entity model that governs how a band source resolves to member shares is never read.

findings.claim: Two boundary questions are marked with a bare `[PENDING]` carrying neither an owner nor a deferral target. One of them decides whether a category the domain forbids from auto-approval can be reached by an auto-approved request.
findings.evidence: 11.11-grand-rights-dramatic-performance.md:54: 'Where does a concert with staging sit? | The boundary between a dramatic performance and a theatrical concert is genuinely contested | `[PENDING]` - not something the platform should adjudicate.' The file's own D-02 (line 90) makes the boundary load-bearing: 'Grand rights are never auto-approvable | No writer ticking "auto-approve under £500" means "you may stage a musical"', reinforced by its edge case at line 53 - 'Grand rights must be excluded from any auto-approve default, or the policy silently grants something enormous.' Its three Open Questions (lines 98-100) are all resolved and none covers the classification. 11.09-cover-song-compulsory-mechanical.md:58 is the second instance: 'Cover is a parody | Different legal analysis entirely (fair use / fair dealing), and out of scope | `[PENDING]` - not something the platform should adjudicate.' Both stand in contrast to the tree's own convention everywhere else, e.g. 11.01.04:56 - '`[PENDING - /create-prd: owner hold-window ceiling - this is Q-03, answer once]`'.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent who classifies a staged concert, since the platform declines to and no other actor is named.
findings.failureScenario: A theatre requests a licence for a 'staged concert' of a work whose writer set an auto-approve policy under £500. If the request classifies as ordinary live performance, 11.04.01's policy fires and the licence auto-approves. If it classifies as grand rights, 11.11 D-02 forbids auto-approval absolutely. The `[PENDING]` says the platform will not decide and names no party who will, so the classification defaults to whatever the requester declared - which is precisely the silent enormous grant 11.11's edge case exists to prevent.
